title: Where one person's fasting glucose lands, on the same horizontal scale
alt: A wide bell curve centred on 142 mg/dL spreading from about 88 to 196, with the band from 124 to 160 shaded.
longDescription: Each point on the horizontal axis is a fasting glucose reading one adult in the cohort could have. The curve is centred on 142 mg/dL with a standard deviation of 18 mg/dL, the figure computed from the sixty readings in the lesson on centre and spread. The shaded band runs from 124 to 160 mg/dL, one standard deviation either side of 142, and holds roughly two thirds of the people. The curve still has visible height at 106 and at 178, two standard deviations out, and the cohort's real readings did run from about 100 to 181. The horizontal axis runs from 88 to 196 mg/dL, exactly the range used for the chart of repeat cohort means, and the difference between the two pictures is the whole point of this lesson: this curve fills the range, while the curve of repeat means occupies a strip about 14 mg/dL wide near the middle of it. The ratio of the two widths is 18 divided by 2.32, which is 7.75, the square root of 60. The vertical axis is relative frequency with no units, and it is scaled to this curve's own peak, so compare the two charts by width and not by height.

shadedRegions.label: One standard deviation either side of 142: 124 to 160 mg/dL
